key_insight: A continuous diffusion language model replaces random latent-to-text mapping to generate more natural attack prompts while retaining Gaussian latent-space sampling and optimization.
engineering_relevance: Learned language mappings can make black-box LLM stress tests more realistic and materially change estimated model risk.
method: Map standard-Gaussian latent variables to text using a continuous diffusion language model.
Evaluate sampling-based risk estimation with RareTrap.
Evaluate optimization-based attack search with ThinkTrap.
evidence_signal: Character-level perplexity falls from 10^3–10^7 to 3–5 in RareTrap and from 20–28 to 4.3–5.4 in ThinkTrap; risk estimates can differ by an order of magnitude between mappings.
watch_item: Lower perplexity alone does not establish guardrail evasion or representative real-world risk.
paper_title: Diffusion Language Models for Perplexity-Aware Black-Box Attacks
